title: Prove a proposed MPMC lock-free queue is linearizable

provenance.notes: Chosen because it is genuinely hard, yet a model checker gives an independent mechanical oracle — the property that lets returnPolicy be complete-only. Contrast with 'startup strategy', which has no such oracle and would be forced to strongest-partial-allowed.

ontology.definition: Every concurrent history is equivalent to some legal sequential history in which each operation appears to take effect atomically at a single instant between its invocation and its response.
A FIFO queue with multiple concurrent producers and consumers.
The single instant at which an operation's effect becomes visible to all threads.

objective.claim: The proposed enqueue/dequeue algorithm (see artifactToVerify) is linearizable under a sequentially consistent memory model within the bounded model checked by TLC: up to 3 concurrent producers, up to 3 concurrent consumers, and queue capacity 4. The unbounded case is explicitly out of scope (see nonGoals).
objective.claimFormalization: TLA+ property: Spec => Linearizable, checked exhaustively by TLC over the bounded model (<= 3 producers, <= 3 consumers, queue capacity 4). TLC over the full bounded state space is SOUND for this bounded claim.

success.successCriterion: A machine-checked TLA+ model of the algorithm for which TLC reports no violation of the Linearizable property across the FULL bounded state space (<= 3 producers, <= 3 consumers, capacity 4) with no state-space truncation.
nonGoals: Passing stress tests or fuzzing — observing no failure is not a proof of linearizability.
Linearizability of only enqueue OR only dequeue in isolation.
A model that silently assumes a single producer or single consumer.
Correctness under a stronger memory model than the one claimed, presented as if it settled the claim.
Extrapolating the bounded TLC result to unbounded producers/consumers — the bounded model check does not establish the unbounded claim, and this spec deliberately does not assert it.

approaches.name: explicit-linearization-points
approaches.lens: Assign a concrete linearization point to each op and prove histories reorder to it.

approaches.name: refinement-mapping
approaches.lens: Build a refinement mapping from the implementation spec to an atomic-queue spec.

approaches.name: separation-logic-invariant
approaches.lens: Derive a rely-guarantee / concurrent-separation-logic invariant that entails linearizability.
approaches.seedIdea: Track per-node ownership transfer on the CAS that publishes a node.

approaches.name: happens-before-order
approaches.lens: Reason directly over the happens-before relation induced by the CAS/load-acquire edges.

search.crossPollinationRule: After round 2, let the refinement-mapping route borrow linearization points found by the operational route, but only once each has an independently checked partial model.
search.blockedRouteReopenRule: Reopen a blocked route only when a new invariant or a new linearization-point assignment is proposed — not merely a re-run of TLC on the same model.
antiProgressRules: A model that restricts to <= 1 producer or <= 1 consumer is equivalent in strength to a much weaker claim and does not count as progress.
'TLC found no violation at capacity 1' is not progress toward the general bounded claim.
requiredArtifacts: A concrete linearization-point assignment for enqueue and dequeue.
For any refuted candidate, the TLC counterexample trace.

adversarialChecklist.failureMode: ABA problem masquerading as a valid CAS success.
adversarialChecklist.check: Add a version/tag to pointers in the model and re-check that the CAS still linearizes.

adversarialChecklist.failureMode: Lost-enqueue when tail lags behind the true last node.
adversarialChecklist.check: Assert the model advances tail before returning, or that a helper does; look for a trace where a node is unreachable.

adversarialChecklist.failureMode: Dequeue returning a node still logically owned by a producer.
adversarialChecklist.check: Model per-node ownership and assert no two ops claim the same node.

adversarialChecklist.failureMode: Linearization point placed outside the [invocation, response] interval.
adversarialChecklist.check: Assert each chosen point lies within its operation's interval in every history.

verifier.ceiling: Sound only for the stated bound (<=3 producers, <=3 consumers, capacity 4). It establishes nothing about the unbounded case, which is deliberately out of scope (see nonGoals).
verifier.notes: The runner executes this and gates on exit code; a passing agent claim without a passing TLC run is rejected.

forbiddenLookups: whether this specific queue algorithm is already published as linearizable
existing TLA+ models of this exact algorithm
